_meta.idConvention: All ids are real exported ids from lib/materials.ts (reconciled 2026-10-11).
_meta.note: Recovery notes keyed by material id. Notes describe process families and handling only — never yields or prices (see pricing.json for estimates, which are always flagged).

bt-18650.name: 18650 cylindrical cell
bt-18650.recoveryNote: The classic laptop/power-tool Li-ion cell. Discharge to 0 V, then mechanical + hydrometallurgical recovery.

bt-blackmass-li.name: Li-ion black mass
bt-blackmass-li.recoveryNote: Shredded cathode/anode powder — Co, Ni, Li, Mn rich. The payable fraction of a Li-ion pack.

bt-bms.name: Battery management system PCB
bt-bms.recoveryNote: Protection/balancing board in every pack; treat as low-grade PCB.

bt-cr2032.name: CR2032 lithium coin cell
bt-cr2032.recoveryNote: Motherboard CMOS cells. Segregate from the main stream; lithium metal content.

bt-lco.name: LCO (lithium cobalt oxide) cathode
bt-lco.recoveryNote: Phone and laptop cells with high cobalt content — historically the most valuable cathode to recycle.

bt-lfp.name: LFP (lithium iron phosphate) cathode
bt-lfp.recoveryNote: Cobalt-free; lithium is the payable metal. Common in budget EVs, e-rickshaws and storage.

bt-lipoly.name: Li-polymer cell
bt-lipoly.recoveryNote: Gel-electrolyte pouch cells in phones and drones. Puncture/fire risk dominates handling.

bt-nmc811.name: NMC 811 cathode
bt-nmc811.recoveryNote: High-nickel, low-cobalt — nickel and lithium are the payable metals.

bt-pb-case.name: Lead-acid battery case (PP)
bt-pb-case.recoveryNote: Polypropylene contaminated with acid — wash before regrind.

bt-pb-grid.name: Lead-acid battery grid
bt-pb-grid.recoveryNote: Lead-calcium or lead-antimony plate grids. Lead — neurotoxin; authorised smelter only.

bt-pb-paste.name: Lead-acid battery paste
bt-pb-paste.recoveryNote: Lead oxide/sulphate paste on plates — the main lead-bearing fraction.

el-ag.name: Silver
el-ag.recoveryNote: Switch contacts, solders, PV cells, conductive pastes — ~0.35 g per phone.

el-al.name: Aluminium
el-al.recoveryNote: Chassis, heat sinks, electrolytic-capacitor foil, cable shielding. Clean unibody scrap remelts directly.

el-au.name: Gold
el-au.recoveryNote: PCB edge connectors and plating — ~0.03 g per phone. Recovered from populated-board smelting, not manual picking.

el-br.name: Bromine
el-br.recoveryNote: Brominated flame retardants in plastics and PCB laminates (legacy). Restricted substances — segregate.

el-cd.name: Cadmium
el-cd.recoveryNote: Legacy NiCd batteries, CdTe solar, pigments — hazardous. Never landfill.

el-co.name: Cobalt
el-co.recoveryNote: LCO/NMC Li-ion cathodes — a key recovered battery metal. Dust is a respiratory hazard.

el-cr.name: Chromium
el-cr.recoveryNote: Chrome plating, stainless steel. Hexavalent chromium in some plating waste is the hazard, not the metal.

el-cu.name: Copper
el-cu.recoveryNote: Wiring, PCB traces, motor windings — the backbone metal of e-waste. Granulate cables; smelt boards.

el-fe.name: Iron
el-fe.recoveryNote: Steel chassis, transformer and motor cores, ferrite magnets. The bulk weight fraction of most appliances.

el-hg.name: Mercury
el-hg.recoveryNote: CCFL backlights, tilt switches, relays — hazardous. One broken CCFL lamp contaminates a whole batch.

el-in.name: Indium
el-in.recoveryNote: ITO transparent conductors in LCD touchscreens. Present only as thin films — recovered at refiner scale.

el-li.name: Lithium
el-li.recoveryNote: Li-ion battery cathodes and electrolyte salts — the key battery metal. Reactive; water contact is dangerous.

el-mg.name: Magnesium
el-mg.recoveryNote: Magnesium-alloy (AZ91) laptop and phone chassis castings. Flammable as fine turnings — no open grinding.

el-mn.name: Manganese
el-mn.recoveryNote: LMO/NMC cathodes, steel alloying, alkaline-battery cathodes.

el-nd.name: Neodymium
el-nd.recoveryNote: NdFeB magnets in motors, speakers and hard drives — the key recovered rare earth. Segregate magnets before shredding.

el-ni.name: Nickel
el-ni.recoveryNote: NiMH and NMC batteries, plating underlayer, stainless steel.

el-pb.name: Lead
el-pb.recoveryNote: Lead-acid batteries, legacy solder, CRT funnel glass — hazardous. Authorised smelter only.

el-pd.name: Palladium
el-pd.recoveryNote: MLCC electrodes, connector plating — a key recovered precious metal.

el-sb.name: Antimony
el-sb.recoveryNote: Antimony-trioxide flame-retardant synergist in legacy plastics; hardens lead battery grids.

el-si.name: Silicon
el-si.processFamily: no economic recovery at device scale
el-si.recoveryNote: Semiconductor dies and solar cells. Dies are trace mass — recovery is via whole-board smelting.

el-sn.name: Tin
el-sn.recoveryNote: Solder alloys, tin plating, ITO. Recovered with the solder stream.

el-ti.name: Titanium
el-ti.recoveryNote: Premium phone frames, fasteners. Segregate; contaminates aluminium melts.

el-w.name: Tungsten
el-w.recoveryNote: Filaments, phone vibration-motor weights, carbide tooling.

el-zn.name: Zinc
el-zn.recoveryNote: Galvanizing, brass, alkaline batteries, die-cast Zamak housings.

fx-concrete.name: Concrete counterweight
fx-concrete.recoveryNote: Front-load washer counterweight — inert; crush for aggregate.

fx-pcb-shred.name: Populated PCB fraction
fx-pcb-shred.recoveryNote: Shredded or whole populated boards — copper plus Au/Ag/Pd credits at the smelter. Grade matters: mainboards > PSU boards > peripheral boards.

fx-lcd-glass.name: LCD panel glass
fx-lcd-glass.recoveryNote: Thin glass with ITO, polarisers and (in CCFL units) mercury lamps. No melt value — handle as special waste.

dp-crt-funnel.name: Leaded CRT funnel glass
dp-crt-funnel.recoveryNote: ~20–25% lead oxide. Cannot go to normal glass recycling — lead smelter feed or hazardous landfill.

gl-sodalime.name: Soda-lime panel glass
gl-sodalime.recoveryNote: Unleaded CRT panel glass — usable as aggregate, not container glass.

nf-brass-c360.name: Brass
nf-brass-c360.recoveryNote: Connectors, fittings. Segregate from copper for full value.

fe-ss304.name: Stainless steel
fe-ss304.recoveryNote: Washer drums, fasteners. Segregate from carbon steel — worth ~4x.

fe-carbon-steel.name: Carbon steel
fe-carbon-steel.recoveryNote: The bulk fraction of large appliances and desktop cases. Magnetic separation after shredding.

pl-abs.name: ABS
pl-abs.recoveryNote: The default housing plastic for monitors, printers, TVs and small appliances.

pl-hips.name: HIPS
pl-hips.recoveryNote: Refrigerator liners, TV cabinets, disposable housings.

pl-hips-fr.name: Flame-retarded HIPS
pl-hips-fr.recoveryNote: CRT-era TV cabinets with brominated flame retardants — check additive content before regrind.

pl-pc.name: Polycarbonate
pl-pc.recoveryNote: Transparent covers, optical discs, safety glazing.

pl-pc-abs.name: PC/ABS blend
pl-pc-abs.recoveryNote: Premium housings needing toughness + heat resistance (laptops, automotive electronics).

pl-pom.name: Acetal / POM
pl-pom.recoveryNote: Precision gears, printer mechanisms, sliding parts.

pl-pp.name: Polypropylene
pl-pp.recoveryNote: Battery cases, washing-machine tubs, fan blades, living-hinge parts.

pl-pu-foam.name: Polyurethane foam
pl-pu-foam.recoveryNote: Refrigerator insulation. Legacy foam may carry ozone-depleting blowing agents.

pl-pvc.name: PVC
pl-pvc.recoveryNote: Cable insulation, wire jackets, some housings; chlorine content matters in thermal processing — segregate.

pl-pvc-cable.name: PVC cable jacketing
pl-pvc-cable.recoveryNote: The outer sheath of most power and data cables — granulate with the copper.

sd-sac305.name: SAC305 lead-free solder
sd-sac305.recoveryNote: The standard lead-free electronics solder for reflow and wave.

sd-sn63pb37.name: Sn63/Pb37 eutectic solder
sd-sn63pb37.recoveryNote: Classic leaded electronics solder; legacy equipment. Fume extraction when desoldering.
